classification.difficultyReason: Select the nonzero ground-level intercept, simplify with the double-angle identity and connect the sine maximum to the optimal launch angle.

content.prompt:
With the Cartesian equation, we can derive the general equation for the range of a projectile.

Using $y=-\dfrac{gx^2}{2V^2}\sec^2\theta+x\tan\theta$, show, using the properties of the sine graph, that the range of an object projected from ground level is $x=\dfrac{V^2}{g}\sin 2\theta$, and explain why the maximum range occurs at an angle of projection of $45^\circ$.

answer.short: $x=\dfrac{V^2}{g}\sin 2\theta$. The maximum range is $\dfrac{V^2}{g}$, attained when $\sin 2\theta=1$, so $\theta=45^\circ$.
answer.worked:
At ground level, $y=0$. For the landing point, $x\ne0$.

$$\begin{align*}x\tan\theta&=\frac{gx^2}{2V^2}\sec^2\theta\\x&=\frac{2V^2\tan\theta}{g\sec^2\theta}\\x&=\frac{2V^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}\\x&=\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{g}.\end{align*}$$

The sine graph has $-1\le\sin 2\theta\le1$, so the maximum range is $\dfrac{V^2}{g}$. It occurs when

$$\begin{align*}\sin 2\theta&=1\\2\theta&=90^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ.\end{align*}$$
